here and not on `CreateBenefitBaseRequest` — the Journey-admin twin
derives the strategy the same way it always has, and `forbidNonWhitelisted`
turns an admin sending this into a 400 rather than a silent drop.

`propertyInternal`, `award` → `requireApproval`), so existing HXP callers
are unchanged. Supplied, it must be in the two-slug partner allowlist;
`external` gets its own message because it is display-only and excluded
from the entitlement read view.

The type includes `null` because that is what actually arrives: `@IsOptional()`
short-circuits validation for null as well as undefined, and `whitelist`
keeps a decorated property, so a client serialising an unset optional as
`"fulfillmentStrategy": null` reaches the service with null intact. Null is
treated as "no choice made" — identical to omitting the field.

`forbidNonWhitelisted` turns an admin sending this into a 400 rather than
a silent drop.

Optional so existing HXP callers keep working, but REQUIRED the moment
`memberVisible` is true — enforced in `BenefitDefinitionService`, not here,
because an update can flip visibility without resending the title.

benefits should be private: most should be shown. What the default buys is
that forgetting to write guest copy yields an unpublished benefit rather
than a published internal note.

`rateCodeOverride` to vary it per tier, which is the normal case: one
"Member rate" benefit whose code differs at each rung of the ladder.

These are not ordinary benefits: Core's resolvers look them up directly by
`system_key`, never by scanning a partner's benefits or matching a name.

moving the marker after members have been promised a rate changes what
they were promised. Re-author the definition instead.

One field rather than two booleans so "both at once" is unrepresentable
rather than a validation error, and so an authoring UI is one control.

info.description:
REST API for Journey partner integrations.

## Base URL

Every path below already includes the `/v1` version prefix.

## Authentication

Send either a WorkOS access token as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` or a Journey API key as
`X-API-Key: jny_...`. `X-API-Key` is evaluated first. The organization a request is scoped to
is always derived from the credential.

## Required scopes

Each operation carries an `x-required-scopes` extension: an array of groups, where **every group
must be satisfied (AND)** and **any one scope within a group satisfies it (OR)**.

For example `[["partner:guests:read"], ["partner:guests:pii:read"]]` means the credential must hold
both scopes, while `[["partner:loyalty:programs:read"]]` means it must hold that single scope.
An empty array means the operation enforces no scope beyond authentication.

## Errors

Errors share one body shape: `type`, `timestamp`, `code`, `message`, and an optional `details`
object. Validation failures additionally carry an `errors` array. `code` repeats the HTTP status
unless a more specific application code applies.

or duplicate a row when the PMS sync writes underneath the caller, and it

external_reservation_id)` — the PUBLIC reservation uuid, never an internal

request.

one), never a 400 and never a 500: both fields are shape-checked before

wins, and the response then echoes `offset: 0` because that is the offset
